en.title: The WhatsApp bot: nine real chats, three through each menu button
en.subtitle: The chats from 5 October 2026, taken from the WhatsApp inbox. Assaf Clix, the test tenant in בר כוכבא 23 flat 2, wrote to the live bot from your number nine times, three times through each of the three menu buttons, each time with a different problem and mood. Every reply below is exactly what reached the phone.
how: These are real conversations with the live WhatsApp bot on 5 October, 14:57 to 15:41 Israel time, in your own chat (conversation 1 in the inbox). The bot's real code, model (Gemini 2.5 Flash), tools and checks answered every message.

These chats show the bot as it was at 15:41 Israel time on 5 October. Later that evening, between 18:03 and 19:31 Israel time, five fixes went live: a safety net for the bot's last-resort rewrite; a promise filter that cuts only promises; ticket lookups that find the mould and gate tickets, and a balance check that accepts your +63 number when typed; straight answers; and only six emoji. Then, at 20:02, a new "how are you today?" greeting on the representative button. Several problems below are what those fixes aim at; a retest of these chats on the fixed bot has not been run yet.

Assaf Clix is the test tenant: flat 2 in בר כוכבא 23, owing 2,000 ₪ for January to August. His messages were written by Claude, acting as a real tenant in each situation, and sent into the live bot the way WhatsApp delivers a message. That is why they appear here but not on the phone, and not in the inbox.

Everything the bot did was real and was kept: tickets 255-1343-26 (the lift), 255-1344-26 (the bathroom leak), 255-1345-26 (the car-park gate) and 255-1346-26 (the cleaning), and 19 notes to the team in the inbox.
The bot's replies are copied from the inbox. The grey lines say what the bot did with its tools; the shaded rows are its notes to the team, which only staff see in the inbox.
Also in the inbox that day: your own two quick checks (hello, then "talk to a representative"), at the end.
findings: Done right: the menu on every hello; tickets for the lift, the leak, the gate and the cleaning, each with the right building and flat and the number written back; a ticket number typed with spaces was found; the stairwell ticket was found from a description and a date; a neighbour's phone number was refused for privacy; what the 250 ₪ fee covers was explained.
Only 1 of the 9 chats got Assaf everything he came for. 4 got part of it, and 4 got nothing.

It told Assaf three times that it had opened a ticket for the mould, number 255-1345-26 (chat 6). No ticket was opened, and that number is the car-park gate's from earlier in his chat. The note it then sent the team quotes the wrong ticket.
Asked what it is, it said "I'm a large language model, trained by Google" (chat 7) and "I'm Michael, a real customer-service rep at Homies" (chat 3).

It told Assaf the team was updated when no note reached the inbox: the request for the committee minutes and the objection to the renovation (chat 7), "call me back with a time" and "I want a person" (chat 5), and "I updated the team that you want a person" (chat 6). The first three were requests the bot did make, but each came less than a minute after another note, and no note appeared for them.
It gave service times nobody gave it: "up to 4 hours" for an emergency (chat 4) and "up to 3 business days" otherwise (chat 3).
His balance was never checked (chat 8). The bot said it could see the number he was writing from, but demanded it typed "for information security", four times.

"What else can I help you with?" ends almost every reply: after goodbyes, and as the whole answer to "when will they call me?". Assaf: "You keep asking what else you can help with and I still haven't gotten an answer."
"I can't see the earlier reports you opened" (chat 3) was said without looking them up; the building has two open gate tickets.
Some replies were cut mid-sentence by the bot's own promise filter ("...and ask. Shall I update them?", "...as soon as there's news about the cleaning and how often the cleaner comes.").
technical: Source: the WhatsApp inbox (Chatwoot conversation 1, your +63 number), every message of 5 October read through the API, read-only.

Assaf's messages come from the test's own record (scripts/wa_qa.py live; n8n runs 83285 to 83924), because a message injected into the bot is answered but not stored in the inbox. The English for his messages was written with them.
The bot at the time: the live n8n workflow u2JjrbcNPYyyh3yl, Gemini 2.5 Flash on OpenRouter, prompt 65c56f9d9c40 at memory epoch 73.
